findings.note: skills/review-pr-ready/SKILL.md:52 tells the operator that --shard-result and --cross-shard-result 'take precedence over a file of the same identity in resultsDir'. That is false for shard results. internal/shardpack/shardpack.go:306-320 appends explicit paths after the resultsDir listing and dedupes only by resolved path, so a file passed in from elsewhere for a shard that already has a result in resultsDir is ingested as a second result; internal/reviewmanifest/manifest.go:413-416 then raises 'duplicate shard result shard-XX' as a blocker. Following the skill therefore produces a NEEDS_REVISION rather than an override. The precedence claim only happens to hold for the cross-shard result, where Found.CrossShard is a single last-wins pointer (shardpack.go:349-352). Note the source comment at shardpack.go:287 says the opposite of the skill: 'Explicit paths are added to whatever the directory holds.' The identical sentence exists in skills/review-task-done/SKILL.md:50 and needs the same correction.

findings.note: skills/review-pr-ready/SKILL.md:57 promises that after a fix round 'only the edited file's shard and the cross-shard result go ignored: re-review those two and leave the rest.' Shard membership is bucketed by path hash and the bucket is then split by byte budget (internal/contextprofile/shards.go:200-243), so an edit that changes a file's diff size can re-split its bucket and change the hashes of sibling shard-NN-<n> parts, and a change in total diff size changes needBuckets and can reshuffle every shard. The guidance is right in the common case but should not be stated as a guarantee.

evidence.note: invalidation guarantee stated without the re-split caveat
bucket count derives from total diff bytes; sub-shard index derives from per-chunk sizes
